description: From forgotten prototypes to cancelled missions, we dive into the history of NASA's abandoned technologies and tell the story behind them.
summary: As part of NASA’s Space Apps Challenge, which focused on spacecraft abandoned by the agency, we developed “Spacehistory,” an interactive digital flipbook designed to introduce young space enthusiasts to the history of the rovers, landers, and modules left on the Moon and Mars. This digital booklet consists of two main sections (Moon and Mars) that present each space object through a minimalist design, combining its original function, achievements, current condition, and unusual anecdotes—all linked by fluid narrative transitions rather than a simple timeline to make it more engaging to follow. This project directly addresses the challenge’s objective—which focuses on storytelling—by transforming technical archives into captivating stories for children. It highlights the historical legacy of space exploration and sparks the curiosity of new generations about engineering and astronomy.
details: SpaceHistory is an interactive digital book on 13 retired NASA missions, from Surveyor 3 (1967) to Ingenuity (2024). Each mission has its own page covering why it was built, its history, its technology, why and where it stopped, how long it lasted, and how it connects to the others. Readers can browse it as a website or read it as a page turning flipbook, and they can rotate and pull apart 3D models of five spacecraft.
